title: From History to State: Constant-Context Skill Learning for LLM Agents
claim: Learn reusable procedures from successful trajectories into lightweight weights, so inference needs only the current observation and a compact state, not history.
layout: 3 numbered panels, left-to-right, dashed feedback loop in inference panel
description: A three-stage left-to-right pipeline diagram with numbered circular headers. Panel 1, 'From Successful Trajectories to State Blocks', is the largest. It shows a trajectory box (observation/action sequence with icons), a Deterministic State Tracker with subgoal fields (Phase, Visible?, Done?) and global state (Goal, Target, Constr.), and a Compact State Block b_t (Current subgoal, Target, Progress). Below, a row builds the step input x_t from task goal, current observation, one-step context and state block. Panel 2, in purple, trains a frozen base LLM plus a Task-Family LoRA with SFT and RL, and outputs an action. Panel 3, in green, shows inference: constant-size input, frozen LLM plus trained LoRA, action, then environment and tools, with a dashed loop back to the input. A footer reads 'No growing history'. Pastel fills and small icons are used throughout.
caption: Context-to-weights skill learning pipeline.
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used to operate browsers, files, code and tools, making personal assistants a natural deployment target. Yet personal agents face a privacy-cost-capability tension: cloud models execute multi-step workflows well but expose sensitive intermediate context to external APIs, while local models preserve privacy but remain less reliable. Both settings also pay repeatedly for long skill prompts and growing histories. We propose constant-context skill learning, a context-to-weights framework for recurring agent workflows: reusable procedures are learned in lightweight task-family modules, while inference conditions only on the current observation and a compact state block. A deterministic tracker renders this state block from task progress and supplies aligned subgoal rewards, so each module can be trained with step-level SFT and refined through online RL. Across ALFWorld, WebShop, and SciWorld, our agents achieve strong performance across Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, and Llama-3.1-8B. With Qwen3-8B, SFT+RL reaches 89.6% unseen success on ALFWorld, 76.8% success on WebShop, and 66.4% unseen success on SciWorld. They match or exceed strong published agent-training results while reducing prompt tokens per turn by 2-7x relative to controlled ReAct prompting baselines, showing that procedural context can be moved from prompts into weights. Code is available at https://github.com/haoyangxie/constant-context-skill-learning.
